leads.old_text: A [**tuning curve**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} gives a neuron's expected firing rate as a function of a represented variable. For eye angle $\theta$, a simple local model is $r_i(\theta)=b_i+k_i\theta$. Neuron $i$ has baseline rate $b_i$ in spikes per second and slope $k_i$ in spikes per second per degree. The linear expression can describe an active range, but it must be modified where it would predict negative firing. The eye paper includes a firing threshold and terms for movement as well as position.[^f-eye]

leads.old_text: Spatial tuning gives a second example. In the hippocampus, a brain structure involved in memory and navigation, a place cell fires strongly in one or more localized regions of an environment. A connected region of elevated spatial firing is a place field. One neuron can have several fields. A [**rate map**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} estimates the rate at each position by dividing the spikes recorded there by the time spent there. Sparse visits, smoothing, and firing cutoffs therefore affect the estimated map and its fields. A field in a model's expected rate and a field extracted from finite recordings are related objects with different measurement uncertainties.[^f-place]
